historical_claims.anchor: In nineteen fifty-three, he proved that every contraction on a Hilbert space can be represented through the powers of a unitary operator on a suitably larger Hilbert space.

verification.primary_locator: Acta Sci. Math. 15 (1953), printed p. 88, Théorème I and formula (1); original journal PDF page 2 inspected

historical_claims.anchor: In his nineteen forty-seven work on self-adjoint perturbations, Szőkefalvi-Nagy made a major contribution to this problem.
historical_claims.source_locator: Comment. Math. Helv. 19 (1946/47), 347–366; Simon (2018), discussion of unitary relation of close projections

historical_claims.anchor: In nineteen thirty-six Szőkefalvi-Nagy completed his qualification to teach mathematics and physics.
Szőkefalvi-Nagy's early book, published in nineteen forty-two, concerned the spectral representation of linear transformations on Hilbert space.
historical_claims.source_locator: Spektraldarstellung linearer Transformationen des Hilbertschen Raumes (1942)

historical_claims.anchor: In nineteen forty-eight he became a professor and departmental leader at the University of Szeged, a position he held until his retirement in nineteen eighty-three.
historical_claims.source_locator: Municipal honorary citizen record, academic appointments

historical_claims.anchor: In nineteen fifty-two, he and Frigyes Riesz published Leçons d'analyse fonctionnelle, a large text on functional analysis.
Their joint work led to a sequence of papers and to a major book published in French in nineteen sixty-seven, later known in English as Harmonic Analysis of Operators on Hilbert Space.
He received several major honors, including the Lomonosov Gold Medal in nineteen seventy-nine.
